geometry.polygon: Horizontal staff / long rectangle: heels-to-crown line parallel to floor, wrists as front posts
geometry.summary: From hands and toes (or knees), stack wrists under shoulders and lengthen one continuous line from heels through pelvis and crown, roughly parallel to the floor. Elbows soft-straight, not locked. Hips neither pike nor sag. The shape is a held horizontal staff: four contact points (two hands, two feet) supporting a long midline.
geometry.svg_hint: side view: two wrist posts under shoulders, long horizontal body bar heels-to-crown, toes tucked, head in line with spine looking slightly ahead of hands

reaction.name: Hold-line
reaction.summary: School metaphor: shaky, piece-by-piece effort reorganizes into one steady horizontal charge along the central line. Not a biochemical claim.

breath.lands_in: midline core band (navel to low ribs) without collapsing the plank line
breath.cue: Equal inhale four, exhale four. Keep the breath quiet and even so the line does not bounce or sag. No forced retention.

orientation.cue: Wrists under shoulders; heels press back; crown reaches forward so heels-to-head stay one long line.
orientation.gravity: Body parallel to the floor; press the floor away through the hands; lift the front of the thighs and lower belly so the hips do not dump.
orientation.gaze: Soft toward the floor a short way ahead of the hands; neck stays in line with the spine.
orientation.degrees_hint: Torso ~0° to floor (true plank); avoid piking hips above ~20° or sagging belly below the line.

attention.primary: Central line from heels through crown
attention.secondary: Wrists stacked under shoulders; even press through both hands

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Twelve successive centers, linked with twelve letters, are meditated in turn—first in a coarse phase, then subtle, then supreme—each left behind until, in the end, identification with Śiva is pointed to.
adiyogi.method_summary: Safe class form in plank: move attention up a short midline sequence (pelvic floor → navel → heart → throat → brow). At each station, feel the coarse body-sense, then a subtler quiet, then leave it and rise to the next. Do not drill genital-tip (janmāgra) stations. No forced breath-hold; keep equal breath while the attention climbs and releases.

honesty.disclosure: This asana↔method link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not ancient canon. Plank is paired with VBT dharana 007 by school index, not by historical one-to-one tradition.
honesty.notes: Mild experiential rhyme only: plank holds a continuous midline while dharana 007 moves attention station-to-station along central stations and leaves each. Classical verse 30 includes janmāgra (generative tip); School class form omits that station and starts at pelvic floor / navel. That rhyme and omission do not upgrade pairing beyond school_device.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: Drop knees to the floor (knee plank), elevate hands on blocks or a chair, or take a short hold and rest in Child's Pose. Wrists may turn slightly outward or use fists/forearms if hands complain—keep the long line.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Ease out if wrists, shoulders, or low back turn sharp. Do not sag or pike through pain. Shorten the hold rather than collapse the line. Pregnancy and wrist concerns: prefer knee plank, elevated hands, or skip the hold.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This door is Plank, Phalakasana. A held horizontal staff—heels to crown in one long line over the hands.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: Wrists under shoulders. Press the floor away. Lengthen heels back and crown forward so the body is one plank, not a pike or a sag.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Body parallel to the floor. Gaze soft ahead of the hands. Neck stays in line. Lift the front thighs and lower belly into the line.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Inhale four, exhale four. Six easy cycles. Keep the breath quiet so the plank line does not bounce. No forced holds.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Lock on the central line from heels through crown. Secondary: even press through both hands under the shoulders.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: Feel the school cue called Hold-line: wobbling scatter becomes one continuous midline. Metaphor only—not a medical claim.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Adiyogi thread, safe form: walk attention up pelvic floor, navel, heart, throat, brow. Feel each, then leave it and rise. Soft equal breath—no genital-station drills.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Lower the knees, or step back to Down Dog, or rest in Child's Pose. Shake out the wrists. Carry the long midline into the next shape. Pain means pause or exit.
